See also: Dolce and dolĉe

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian dolce. Doublet of douce, doux, and dulce.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈdoʊl.tʃeɪ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

dolce (plural dolces)

  1. (music) A soft-toned organ stop.

Related terms

[edit]
  • dolce far niente
  • dolce stil nuovo
  • dolce vita
  • la dolce vita

Anagrams

[edit]
  • codel, codle, colde, coled

Asturian

[edit]

Numeral

[edit]

dolce (indeclinable)

  1. alternative form of doce (“twelve”)

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin dulcem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈdol.t͡ʃe/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -oltʃe
  • Hyphenation: dól‧ce

Adjective

[edit]

dolce m or f by sense (plural dolci, superlative dolcissimo)

  1. sweet
  2. gentle, mild
  3. luscious, sooth
  4. dear
  5. (phonetics) soft

Derived terms

[edit]
  • chi ha l'amaro in bocca, non può sputar dolce (proverb)

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Esperanto: dolĉa

See also

[edit]
Basic tastes in Italian · sapori (layout · text)
dolce acido, aspro salato amaro piccante saporito, gustoso

Noun

[edit]

dolce m (plural dolci)

  1. sweetness
  2. dessert
  3. cake

Related terms

[edit]
  • addolcire
  • dolcemente
  • dolcetto
  • dolcezza
  • dolciario
  • dolcificante
  • dolcificare
  • dolciume

Lombard

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin dulcis.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Old Lombard) IPA(key): [ˈdolt͡se]

Adjective

[edit]

dolce

  1. (Old Lombard) sweet

Polish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈdɔl.t͡sɛ/
  • Rhymes: -ɔlt͡sɛ
  • Syllabification: dol‧ce

Noun

[edit]

dolce

  1. nominative/accusative/vocative plural of dolec

Romanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Unadapted borrowing from Italian dolce.

Adverb

[edit]

dolce

  1. dolce
